worked_example.problem: Explain why {p} moved into northern Cameroon.
steps: They were cattle herders looking for good pasture and water.
In the {'19th'} century the jihad led by Modibo Adama spread Islam and Fulani rule southwards, creating the Adamawa emirate.
worked_example.answer: Pasture for their cattle, and the {'19th'}-century jihad of Modibo Adama.

cards.idea: Bantu peoples live mostly in the South and along the coast.
Semi-Bantu peoples live in the Grassfields; Sudanese peoples and the Fulani in the north.
People migrated to find land and pasture, to escape wars, and during the Fulani jihad.
example: Modibo Adama led the jihad from {y}.

pick.q: Who led the Fulani jihad in northern Cameroon from 1809?
e: Njoya was a later Bamum ruler.
King Bell was a Duala chief.
Adama was a follower of Usman dan Fodio.
pick.y: Modibo Adama founded the Adamawa emirate.

pick.q: Which was a cause of migration in Cameroon?
pick.r: the search for fertile land and pasture
pick.y: Land, pasture, wars and the jihad moved people.

pick.q: Why did many Sudanese peoples settle in the Mandara mountains?
pick.r: to take refuge from Fulani and slave raids
e: The mountains are far from the sea.
pick.y: The mountains were easier to defend.

right.text: The Duala are a Bantu people.
The Bamileke live in the Grassfields.
The Mafa live in the north.

wrong.text: The Fulani arrived in the 20th century.
wrong.explain: They arrived mainly in the 18th and 19th centuries.

wrong.text: The Bakweri are a Sudanese people of the far north.

wrong.text: Modibo Adama led the Bamum kingdom.
